The [AAA](https://whatpr.org/html/12756/f9a87e5...7e7d89d/parsing.html#adoption-agency-algorithm) seems to still create elements from tokens and insert without sanitizing. (Steps 4.13.8 and 4.18.)

[Speculative parsing](https://whatpr.org/html/12756/f9a87e5...7e7d89d/parsing.html#speculative-html-parsing) also needs to sanitize (or be disabled). Otherwise elements that would be removed by the sanitizer can affect speculative fetches (`base`, `meta`) or can cause speculative fetches (e.g. `img`, `script`).

Similarly https://whatpr.org/html/12756/f9a87e5...7e7d89d/parsing.html#create-an-element-for-the-token step 2 should not cause a speculative fetch if the sanitizer would remove the element or some attributes.

I think doing something similar to https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/12758/changes#diff-41cf6794ba4200b839c53531555f0f3998df4cbb01a4d5cb0b94e3ca5e23947dR145542-R145556 in https://whatpr.org/html/12756/f9a87e5...7e7d89d/parsing.html#create-a-speculative-mock-element before step 6 would work. (The sanitizer would need to accept a speculative mock element, but maybe [this text](https://whatpr.org/html/12756/f9a87e5...7e7d89d/parsing.html#speculative-mock-element:~:text=DOM%20operations%20that%20the%20tree%20builder%20normally%20does%20on%20elements%20are%20expected%20to%20work%20appropriately%20on%20speculative%20mock%20elements%2E) is already sufficient.)

I don't think this is an issue at all. The sanitizer only works on parsers associated with inactive documents (either because it's `parseHTML`, or it's a fragment parser). Those documents cannot fetch or queue tasks etc.

If this was an issue, it would be an existing one.
